evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/voting/pages/VotingPage.tsx:8-11 — the voting LIST page imports neither useTranslation nor any i18n helper (only api-client hooks, Spinner, VoteCard, and VOTE_STATUS_LABELS), and every user-facing string is a hardcoded English literal: the <h1> 'Voting' (line 54), the summary line '{n} vote{s} · {open} open · {closed} closed' (55-58), the '+ New vote' button (66), the 'All' filter label (81), the error state 'Failed to load votes: … Unknown error' (94-95), the empty state 'No votes yet.' (100) and 'Create the first vote' CTA (104). None go through t().

This is a localization REGRESSION, not merely an un-i18n'd new screen: the two sibling pages in the same feature — VoteCreatePage.tsx and VoteDetailPage.tsx — both use useTranslation (2 of 3 voting pages localized), and the feature ships an explicit i18n contract test, frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/voting/pages/VoteDetailPage.i18n.test.tsx. The list page was left out of that contract, so on a portal whose managers can run in sk/cs/de/en the whole voting entry screen renders English regardless of the selected UI language.

Impact: user-facing untranslated UI on a first-class Epic-5 manager screen (screen id ppt/voting). Severity low (i18n gap — no crash, no data loss), confidence medium (confirmed by static read: no i18n import present and literals are inline JSX; the multi-locale requirement is documented in CLAUDE.md — reality/ppt support sk/cs/de/en). Fix is fully cloud-landable: add useTranslation, move the ~8 literals into the existing ppt-web message catalog under a voting.* namespace (mirroring VoteDetailPage's keys), and route VOTE_STATUS_LABELS through t(). Secondary observation for the fixer (do not file separately): line 30 buildingId = buildingsData?.items?.[0]?.id ?? '' silently pins the vote query to the first building with no building selector — a known ppt-web pattern, note only.

Confirmed hardcoded English in frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/forms/pages/AvailableFormsPage.tsx:

'Available Forms'

(line 63), 'All Categories' option (74), and the empty state 'No forms available' (130). The other four form pages share the same no-i18n-import shape.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/government-portal/pages/GuestReportSubmissionPage.tsx has the same defect on a HIGHER-stakes surface: it is the regulatory guest-registration wizard that submits to Slovak government portals (its own copy names 'ÚHÚL/Police', line 222), yet every label is hardcoded English — <h1>'Submit Guest Report' (220), the subtitle (222), the wizard step labels ['Select Options','Preview Data','Submit'] (229), and the section headers 'Select Country' (315), 'Portal Connection' (350), 'Report Template' (396), 'Submission Preview' (514). A compliance flow aimed at Slovak operators rendering only English is a usability/adoption risk beyond a cosmetic gap.

Impact: a whole feature (forms) plus a regulatory government-portal flow are untranslated on a documented multi-locale (sk/cs/de/en) portal. Severity low per the finding taxonomy (i18n gap, no crash), but breadth is high — 6 pages, one of them regulatory. Confidence medium (confirmed by static read: absent i18n imports + inline English literals; multi-locale requirement per CLAUDE.md). Fully cloud-landable: wire useTranslation into each page and lift the strings into the ppt-web catalog. Recommend splitting the implementation into two plan-sized chunks (forms.* and governmentPortal.*) if a single PR would exceed review size.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/compliance/pages/ContentModerationPage.tsx:203-208 — handleViewContent navigates to an INTERNAL route with a hard document navigation: `window.location.href = `/compliance/moderation/cases/${caseId}``, guarded by its own TODO 'Use React Router's useNavigate for SPA navigation / Phase 1: Full page reload for simplicity'. Every 'view content' click on a moderation case tears down and re-boots the whole React SPA (re-runs bootstrap, re-fetches auth/building context, drops in-memory TanStack Query cache and the moderation list scroll/filter state) instead of a client-side transition — a measurable UX and performance regression on a manager tool with list-of-cases drill-in.

Same file line 281 — the error-state retry uses `onClick={() => window.location.reload()}`, a full document reload to recover from a query error where a TanStack Query refetch() would suffice; consistent with the same anti-pattern.

Impact: degraded SPA UX (full reloads on internal navigation), not a crash or security issue. Severity low, confidence medium (confirmed by static read; the route target /compliance/moderation/cases/:caseId is an internal SPA route, so client navigation is the correct mechanism). Fully cloud-landable: replace window.location.href with useNavigate() from react-router-dom (already the app's router) and swap the retry's window.location.reload() for the query's refetch(); removes the acknowledged Phase-1 shortcut.
